subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when required exec-backed SecretRefs fail under a service manager that may restart the gateway repeatedly?
rationale: Changing this path affects credential-provider execution, startup fail-closed behavior, external account rate limits, and whether OpenClaw adds config surface or defaults that alter existing deployments.

options.title: Generic bounded startup retry/degrade policy
options.body: Add provider-agnostic bounded retry/backoff or a clear non-restartable degraded startup state, with operator-visible errors and no 1Password-specific core hardcoding.

options.title: Configurable retry/circuit policy
options.body: Add an explicit secrets retry or circuit-breaker configuration surface, accepting the compatibility and docs burden of new startup behavior knobs.

options.title: Docs/plugin workaround only
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast behavior and direct 1Password users to ClawHub/Varlock-style resolvers plus supervisor guidance, accepting that OpenClaw core will not absorb this failure mode.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup retry/degrade policy
recommendation.body: Add provider-agnostic bounded retry/backoff or a clear non-restartable degraded startup state, with operator-visible errors and no 1Password-specific core hardcoding.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history connection to the external SecretRef provider and eager runtime snapshot path that this decision would change.
